statement: The draft is a solid, honest merge, but it is written for operators and auditors. Of its 106 events only about a third are things a team would ever see, and the merges sometimes erased words users actually say (reminder, chat, resume). I want every event marked as either team-visible or internal, a per-channel and per-workspace activity view built from the team-visible ones, and undo that is offered only for what can really be undone, explained in plain sentences.

renames.why: Every process evaluates workspace.eyg on its own (the process boundary rule), so 'evaluated' would fire constantly and means nothing to users. What people need is the moment a saved version took effect, and for which parts: channel config applies on the next message, connections and crons only on restart. Today 'saved' and 'in effect' are silently different, and this event makes the gap visible.
The agent's tool is `run`, which runs an EYG program. Teams say 'the agent ran some code', and this event should link to the run in `runs`. 'Tool call' is model-provider vocabulary.

Binding is an effect that can also come from POST /api/Bind, not only from the web shell. The product glossary calls it Binding and the person is the actor. It needs an end event to pair with (see missing).

splits.why: These are two different things to users: 'remind Alice in 3 minutes her tea is ready' (Timeout, once) and 'post the weekly summary every Monday' (Cron and config crons). They are cancelled, missed and caught up differently (H19), and the activity view should say 'reminder' and 'schedule', not 'timer armed'.

Connecting Slack, Discord or WhatsApp brings channels, people and conversations into the workspace, and messages can start agents. Connecting GitHub, Sentry or a webhook only feeds events to one channel's triggers. The product glossary and the example workspace keep these apart ('GitHub is not a chat, nothing posted on GitHub runs code'), and users judge the risk of each very differently.

missing.why: StartTrigger exists. Pausing a noisy trigger and turning it back on is the most common undo a team does, and the history must show who paused it and who resumed it.
Users want 'bring back this one file', not a restore of the whole file system. Because old roots are kept it is cheap, and it is the human-sized undo for files.
A binding is a window in which a person acted with a channel's powers. Without an end event, the channel history cannot show when that window closed.

Connections get removed from workspace.eyg or lose their secret (the Sentry connection is dropped when SENTRY_CLIENT_SECRET is deleted). 'Why did #dev stop getting GitHub events?' is a real support question, and this answers it.

People delete and edit messages on Slack, Discord and WhatsApp. If the cloud keeps the text forever after the author deleted it, users will see a broken promise, and this event is the natural entry to erasure (H6).

remove.why: This is a command, not a fact. Today a person picks a shell from the dropdown or an admin calls SetUserShell, and either way the fact is PersonShellAssigned, with the person as actor when they chose it themselves. A rejected attempt is an EffectDenied in `runs`.
H8 says to upcast when reading, not to rewrite history. Upcasting is then something the code does, not something that happened, and it would fill the log with entries no human can act on.

context_changes.change: Rename the `conversations` context to `channels` (Channels and agents). Keep 'session' as an internal word.
context_changes.why: Users talk about channels, threads and the agent in #general, and nobody says 'session'. The product glossary defines Channel as the thing with its own agent conversation, triggers and shell.

context_changes.change: Add an explicit Activity read model per channel and per workspace, and tag every event as team-visible or internal. Team-visible: MessagePosted, AgentReplied, AgentStayedQuiet, AgentRanProgram, SubagentDelegated, EffectDenied, EffectMocked, EffectOutcomeInDoubt, RunFailed, Trigger*, ReminderSet, RecurringScheduleSet, ScheduleFired, ScheduleCancelled, CronOccurrenceMissed, ChatConnected, ServiceConnected, ServiceDisconnected, WebhookDeliveryRejected, File*, ArtifactVersionSaved, ArtifactShared, DataclipInvoked, Workspace*, SecretSet, SecretRotated, SecretDeleted, PersonInvited, PersonShellAssigned, PersonBoundToChannel. Everything else (journal, leases, blocks, pins, checkpoints, upcasting) is internal and reached through drill-down only.
context_changes.why: This is how the system stays simple for users while the log is complete for auditors. The admin page shows the Activity view instead of raw trace trees, and each line is a sentence like 'Bob added the regressions trigger to #dev from the product page', with an Undo button only where one exists.

hotspot_positions.position: Keep EffectPermitted, EffectMocked and EffectDenied as separate events, each carrying the shell CID. EffectPermitted is internal and goes into the journal. Denied and Mocked are team-visible, because 'the agent tried to read secrets and was stopped' is exactly what a channel owner wants to see. When a gate rewrote the input, the activity line says so ('posted, shortened by the channel shell').

Decisions for effects that were already performed are reused, because those effects happened. Any effect not yet performed is checked against the current shell. If permission was revoked in between, the run stops with EffectDenied, and the channel shows 'stopped: permissions changed since this started' instead of failing silently.

Never auto-retry a Post: a missing message is better than a duplicate in the team's chat. Where the platform allows it, reconcile with a client message id. Otherwise record EffectOutcomeInDoubt and show it in the channel's Activity with 'Retry' and 'It was posted' buttons, so a person decides. Idempotent reads like Fetch GET, ReadFile and Events may retry automatically.
Every view labels a mocked result 'answered by the shell, not performed', including the agent's own view of the result. Replay feeds the recorded mock and never performs it.

Keep message text, file contents and fetched bodies out of events: store them as blobs by CID, encrypted with a per-workspace key and, for chat text, a per-author key. Erasure shreds the key. The history line remains, as 'message removed at Alice's request, 2026-11-13'. MessageDeleted on the platform can trigger erasure when the workspace setting asks for it.
Agreed. Traces stay a debugging tool. The admin page gets a History tab built from events, and the trace trees remain for performance questions.

Secret values never appear in events or in any view. People see 'OLLAMA_API_KEY replaced by Alice'. Configuration revert cannot bring back an old secret value, and the UI must say so rather than pretending to.

Every event carries the full on-behalf-of chain, but views render at most two steps as a sentence: 'Alice, via the #founders agent', 'the regressions trigger in #dev (added by Bob)', 'the 9am standup schedule', 'Carol, acting as #random'. The full chain is one click away. A trigger's or schedule's creator is part of its identity, so runs it starts are attributed to them.

Invite only after bootstrap. CloudBootstrapped records the first admin, who claims the cloud with a one-time code printed by the server instead of 'whoever arrives first'. After that, PersonInvited (by whom, with which shell) comes before PersonSignedUp. A sign-in that does not match an invitation is SignInRejected.

Both are durable, and both are visible in one list per channel with a source label: 'workspace.eyg' or 'added by Bob from the product page / by the #dev agent'. A runtime trigger is an event in the channel's trigger set, not a configuration change. Configured triggers are reviewed code and win a name clash: the runtime one is marked 'shadowed' rather than silently dropped. TriggerSavedToWorkspace promotes one: it emits WorkspaceSourceChanged and retires the runtime copy. Re-submitting a product page card with the same name replaces the trigger as TriggerAdded, and the previous version stays restorable.

A webhook created without a secret shows a persistent warning on the connection and in the product page cards ('anyone with the URL can send events to #dev'). WebhookDeliveryRejected is team-visible with a reason, because 'my GitHub webhook does nothing' is the most common setup problem.

The Activity view shows only deliveries that matched a trigger or were rejected, plus an hourly count ('3,412 log lines, 6 matched'). Whether unmatched deliveries are kept in full, sampled or counted is a per-connection retention setting, so users don't have to think about it.

Recurring schedules fire one catch-up occurrence, labelled late ('the 9am standup, 2 hours late, the cloud was down'), and record the rest as CronOccurrenceMissed. A one-off reminder always fires late rather than never.

Revert is a new change whose content is an older version, never a deletion of history. Before confirming, the UI lists what a revert does not undo: messages posted, requests sent, secret values. Files and artifact versions can be restored separately, and the UI says so. Undo exists for configuration, triggers, schedules, files, artifact versions and shell assignments. Everything else offers 'what happened' and not 'undo'.

new_hotspots.text: Who may read a channel's history? Slack private channels, WhatsApp chats and DMs are private to their members, but admins, the #founders agent with shell.admin and people bound to a channel could all read the Activity view. History visibility needs its own rule, and owning a shell is not enough.

Changes made by an agent (the #founders agent calling SetWorkspaceSource, SetSecret or SetUserShell) carry the product promise 'agents propose, people decide'. Should agent-made configuration changes be proposals that a person confirms, with distinct ConfigurationChangeProposed and ConfigurationChangeApproved events?
A reminder set by an agent belongs to a conversation. After /new resets it, or after the conversation is erased, where does the reminder's message go, and who can still see or cancel it?

Product page cards install triggers by name ('summarise-on-eyes'). Should submitting the same card twice replace the trigger, or be rejected? Users expect replace, but silently replacing a teammate's trigger with the same name loses their work.
